m.s: Cut {beef_chuck} into large 4cm chunks, pat dry and season with salt. Heat a drizzle of oil in a large heavy pot over high heat and brown the beef in batches for 3 to 4 minutes a side until well coloured. Set aside.
Turn the heat down to medium and add a splash of oil. Fry {massaman} for 2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.

Add {coconut}, ½ cup water for every 2 serves, {fishsauce} and {brownsugar}. Return the beef and bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook on low (or in a 160°C oven) for 2 hours, stirring now and then.
Add {potato} in chunks and {onion} in wedges. Simmer with the lid off for 30 to 40 minutes until the potato is tender and the beef falls apart.

Rinse {rice} until the water runs clear. Put it in a saucepan with 1½ times its volume of cold water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, then cover and cook on low for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes so it finishes steaming.
Taste the curry and adjust: more fish sauce for salt, sugar for sweet, a squeeze of {lime} for sour. Serve over the rice, topped with crushed {peanuts} and torn {coriander}.

l: Even better the next day. Pack the peanuts separately so they stay crunchy. Keeps 4 days in the fridge, and it freezes well.
g: Naturally gluten free. Check the curry paste and fish sauce labels.
